controllingAuthority.summary: On an appropriate request the Bureau shall expunge. No court discretion. Tier A under § 4373(a)(1) is not barred by prior or subsequent ineligible convictions provided every other charge in the case is eligible; Tier B under § 4373(a)(2) requires no prior or subsequent convictions that bar eligibility.

eligibleDispositions: Tier A: the case was terminated in favor of the accused, as defined in § 4372(b)
Tier A: one or more violations in the same case and three years since conviction
Tier A: marijuana possession under 16 Del. C. § 4764 or paraphernalia under § 4771, or both in the same case
Tier A: underage possession or consumption of alcohol under 4 Del. C. § 904(e) or (f)
Tier B: one or more misdemeanors, or misdemeanors combined with violations, in the same case, five years since conviction
Tier B: drug possession under 16 Del. C. § 4756, five years since conviction
Tier B: the six listed felonies, ten years since conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later
exclusions: § 4372(f) plus the § 4373(b) list: crimes of domestic violence as defined there, offenses with a child victim, offenses with a vulnerable adult victim, any misdemeanor in subparts A, B, C, or F of subchapter VI of chapter 5, a long enumerated misdemeanor list, and a § 4373(a)(2)c. felony where the victim falls in the first three categories.
No expungement while criminal charges are pending, except that pending charges do not include an alleged violation of 4 Del. C. § 904(e) or (f), 16 Del. C. § 4764(c), or a Title 21 offense.

Five convictions may never be expunged: vehicular assault in the second degree (§ 628A), incest (§ 766), unlawful sexual contact in the third degree (§ 767), coercion (§ 791), and unlawfully dealing with a child (§ 1106).
No expungement while the person is serving incarceration, parole, or probation.

researchSbiProcess.process: The SBI page distinguishes the expungement/pardon enrollment code 27S23V from the personal-use history code 27RVGT; its linked 'Expungement Application' is a one-page service-code/enrollment instruction sheet, not a standalone court petition or an eligibility determination. Initial fee $72. After review, a mandatory-eligible applicant returns signed paperwork within 30 days of receipt with a $75 money order payable to Delaware State Police; otherwise SBI sends discretionary-process information. The second fee is conditional, never presented as unconditional; automatic-relief screening is preserved. The sheet describes online enrollment and a telephone alternative, 1-866-761-8069, requires valid unexpired photo identification and addresses name-change documentation; no unverified mail-in destination is hardcoded; a date in the sheet's URL is not a printed revision.
researchSbiProcess.participantText: For the SBI expungement application process, enroll through the State Police's linked fingerprint service using code 27S23V. The initial application fee is $72. Follow the registration instructions for the appointment or permitted mail-in option and identification. After SBI reviews the application, read its eligibility notice. If SBI says you qualify for mandatory expungement, return the signed paperwork within 30 days after you receive it, together with a $75 money order payable to Delaware State Police. If SBI instead sends discretionary-expungement information, follow that separate court process. Do not use the personal-background-check code 27RVGT as a substitute.

citations: 11 Del. C. § 4374, most recently amended at 85 Del. Laws, c. 142, § 10
controllingAuthority.summary: Discretionary expungement on petition where the petitioner shows manifest injustice from the continued existence and possible dissemination of the record, by a preponderance. The State is a party defendant. Filed in Superior Court where any charge or conviction was disposed of outside Family Court.

eligibleDispositions: one or more misdemeanors not listed in § 4373(b), same case, at least 3 years since conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later, and no prior or subsequent convictions
one or more misdemeanors listed in § 4373(b), same case, at least 7 years, and no prior or subsequent convictions
a felony, at least 7 years, and no prior or subsequent convictions, subject to the (b) exclusions

one or more violations or non-§ 4373(b) misdemeanors in more than one case, at least 5 years since the most recent conviction or release, and no other prior or subsequent convictions that would not be mandatory-eligible standing alone
exclusions: § 4374(b), on top of § 4372(f): a Title 11 felony listed in § 4201(c); 16 Del. C. § 1136; 31 Del. C. § 3913; and a felony conviction involving physical or sexual assault crimes as defined in 31 Del. C. § 309, the Beau Biden Child Protection Act.

Title 21 bar under § 4374(i): no Title 21 motor vehicle offense, or a county or municipal equivalent, except driving after judgment prohibited (21 Del. C. § 2810), reckless driving (§ 4175), and operation of a motor vehicle causing death (§ 4176A). A DUI under 21 Del. C. § 4177 is not expungeable on this route.
No expungement while criminal charges are pending, except the three carve-outs.
No expungement while the person is serving incarceration, parole, or probation.

rules.filing: Assemble the packet in the prescribed order: petition, proposed order, SBI cover letter, then the certified criminal history dated within 45 days. One original plus one copy. rules.feeWaiver: Under § 4372(l), if an outstanding fine or fee is unpaid for reasons other than wilful noncompliance and the person is otherwise eligible, the court may grant the expungement and waive the fines or fees or convert them to a civil judgment.
rules.notice: The expungement clerk emails a copy of the filing to the Attorney General once a case number is assigned. The Attorney General contacts the victim under § 9414(a) and reports the victim's position in the answer.
rules.service: The petitioner serves the Attorney General, who may object or answer within 120 days. The petition pre-prints the Attorney General's three county addresses, which is the service list. If the Attorney General opposes, the petitioner has 30 days to file a response.
rules.participantSignature: The petition is sworn and subscribed before a clerk of court or notary.
rules.notarization: Required. Filing in person means bringing the petition unsigned and signing in front of the notary at the Prothonotary's office. Filing by mail means notarizing first.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement After a Pardon, 11 Del. C. § 4375

citations: Procedure under 11 Del. C. § 4374(c) through (h) and (j)
controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of any crime other than the six excluded, who has since been unconditionally pardoned by the Governor, may petition. Per the enacting synopsis a § 4375 expungement is not restricted by the eligibility requirements or exclusions in § 4374, and crimes ineligible under § 4372(f) become eligible after an unconditional pardon. This is the only route for a § 4201(c) violent felony and for most of the permanent exclusions.

eligibleDispositions: a conviction for any crime other than the six excluded, followed by an unconditional pardon by the Governor
exclusions: § 4375(b): manslaughter (§ 632), murder in the second degree (§ 635), murder in the first degree (§ 636), rape in the second degree (§ 772), rape in the first degree (§ 773), and sexual abuse of a child by a person in a position of trust, authority, or supervision in the first degree (§ 778(1), (2), or (3)).
